items.titleZh: 霍纳称法拉利是唯一能吸引他回归的车队 汉密尔顿力挺瓦塞尔

items.originalTitle: Who slept worst last night: Lewis Hamilton
items.summaryEn: Christian Horner says Ferrari is the one team that could tempt him back into a traditional F1 role, while Lewis Hamilton has backed Fred Vasseur amid growing speculation around Maranello.
detailZh: 昨晚谁睡得最差：刘易斯·汉密尔顿
克里斯蒂安·霍纳表示，法拉利是唯一能吸引他重返一级方程式传统职位的车队，而随着围绕马拉内罗的猜测不断升温，刘易斯·汉密尔顿则表示支持弗雷德·瓦塞尔。
如果有人在2021年阿布扎比站时预测，几年后刘易斯·汉密尔顿会在法拉利车队、并在领队克里斯蒂安·霍纳手下参加一级方程式比赛，恐怕很少有人会认真对待这种说法。不过即便到了2026年巴库站，也几乎没有迹象表明这一局面正在具体成形。
霍纳最近接受《泰晤士报》采访时表示，他完全负担得起一辈子不再工作。然而，他仍然有再回一级方程式闯一闯的冲动。
新的情况——也是在巴库比赛周末登上头条的——是，他不一定会仅仅以投资者的身份回归。霍纳表示，有一支车队可以让他破例，甚至重新以传统意义上的雇员身份回归，那就是法拉利。
让霍纳这样的人成为汉密尔顿的老板，这一前景目前纯属理论上的设想，但鉴于两人的过往，将会制造一种非同寻常的关系。尽管在这个阶段，这种猜测很可能并没有多少实质内容。
这位长期担任红牛车队领队的人即将为他的新书《驾驶》（Drive）展开宣传活动，而几条把他与法拉利联系在一起的高关注度报道，是让他的名字保持热度的好办法。无论法拉利是否有兴趣雇用他，这既能卖书，也能卖票。
至于汉密尔顿本人，他显然对此并不感兴趣。
当天空体育记者克雷格·斯莱特周六晚上在巴库指出霍纳实际上已经举手表态、把自己列为法拉利的候选人，并询问汉密尔顿是否仍然相信车队在瓦塞尔的带领下走在正确的道路上时，得到的回答简短而毫不含糊：“是的。”
事实上，法拉利过去曾多次与霍纳接触。据报道，2010年，当时的想法是把他从米尔顿凯恩斯挖到马拉内罗，作为与阿德里安·纽维打包交易的一部分。而他接受《泰晤士报》采访时精心措辞的表述，显然表明如果法拉利真的决定按下恐慌按钮、解除瓦塞尔的合同，他会非常有兴趣接手。
据天空德国台评论员蒂莫·格洛克所说，他认为这些言论让瓦塞尔陷入了一个不必要的尴尬境地：“瓦塞尔把法拉利带回到了如今的位置。他为车队带来了结构和秩序。现在换掉他、开启下一波动荡，从战略角度来说，对法拉利而言是完全错误的。”
即使法拉利真的在考虑解雇瓦塞尔，为什么偏偏要把缰绳交给霍纳这样的人呢？
这位52岁的人想必会花费一笔不菲的资金——至少按受薪工作的标准来看是这样——而且他也无法提供任何成功的保证。此外，在红牛最后几年期间针对他的指控之后，霍纳仍然是一个有争议的人物。2025年初，在F1赛季启动仪式上，他在O2体育馆迎接他的嘘声表明，他在一些车迷中仍然是一个两极分化的人物。
瓦塞尔明确表示，这些猜测正在成为一种干扰：“霍纳先生正在找工作。这一点人人都知道。到处都知道。”他还说：“在这种情绪和这种氛围下工作并不容易，一天25次被问到同样的问题。对我、对车队的每个人来说，这都是一种不安宁。”
这正是瓦塞尔和法拉利现在应该得到的东西。法拉利领导层公开重申对瓦塞尔的支持，很可能会减少这些猜测。也许约翰·埃尔坎最好给《米兰体育报》打个电话澄清事实；那样就能很快给这个令人厌烦的霍纳话题画上句号。
无论如何，我不认为汉密尔顿目前会因为霍纳而失眠。他有足够多的其他原因让他睡不着。
无论还有什么微乎其微的可能性，能在2026年以某种方式成为世界冠军，如今这基本只剩下数学上的可能了。虽然法拉利也许可以在空气动力学方面，用不了太久就打造出一级方程式最好的赛车，但在动力单元方面缩小与梅赛德斯的差距可能需要更长时间。就连瓦塞尔本人也承认这一点。
而且对汉密尔顿来说，很多事情都在朝着好的方向发展。
在巴塞罗那，他证明了自己即使已年过四十，依然有能力赢得大奖赛。他在车手总冠军积分榜上排名第三，比队友勒克莱尔整整高出20分，后者排名第五。他在2026年的表现回应了2025赛季之后所遭受的一些批评。
然而，在采访中，尽管成绩有所改善，他的公开言论却常常依然带着失落。
夏尔·勒克莱尔，法拉利；刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利
这种模式一周又一周地重复着：比赛期间，汉密尔顿通过车队电台传递的信息完全可以被合理地理解为带着火气。随后，在电视机镜头前，他会花上好几分钟谈论所有出问题的地方，然后几乎是顺带补一句，说法拉利内部一切都非常正常。
然后，一周之后，在下一站大奖赛的媒体日，他会纳闷那些记者怎么可能把他误解得如此严重。
在巴库之后，他抱怨法拉利缺乏极速，提到起步不佳——赛季初法拉利在这方面的表现本来有所进步——并说车队不能自欺欺人，还指出迈凯伦和红牛取得了更大的进展。他说，这 simply 就是一场“相当糟糕的”比赛。除此之外，他还无法让轮胎进入工作温度。早在周六，他就抱怨过“这些愚蠢的轮胎”，称它们“真是让人头疼”：“我们得把一些好轮胎带回来。”
也许只是我的感觉——但不知为何，汉密尔顿和法拉利目前还谈不上是赛车运动中最伟大的爱情故事之一。
毫无疑问，汉密尔顿是一级方程式历史上最成功的车手之一。
汉密尔顿还会再有一个世界冠军吗？法拉利能给他一个冲击第八冠的现实机会吗？我仍然持怀疑态度。
detailEn: Who slept worst last night: Lewis Hamilton
Christian Horner says Ferrari is the one team that could tempt him back into a traditional F1 role, but Lewis Hamilton has backed Fred Vasseur as speculation builds around Maranello

Had anyone predicted in Abu Dhabi in 2021 that, a few years later, Lewis Hamilton would be racing in Formula 1 for Ferrari under team principal Christian Horner, few would have taken that suggestion seriously. Even as of Baku 2026, though, there is little evidence that such a scenario is taking concrete shape.
In a recent interview Horner gave to The Times, he said he can comfortably afford never to work another day in his life. And yet, he still feels the urge to give Formula 1 another go.

What is new — and what generated headlines during the Baku weekend — is that he would not necessarily return only as an investor. There is one team, Horner said, for which he would make an exception and even go back to being, in the traditional sense, an employee: Ferrari.

The prospect, purely theoretical for now, of having Horner, of all people, installed as his boss would create an unusual dynamic for Hamilton given their history. Even if, at this stage, there is probably little substance to the speculation.

The long-time Red Bull team principal is about to embark on a promotional tour for his new book, Drive, and a few high-profile stories linking him with Ferrari are a useful way of keeping his name in the conversation. It sells books and it sells tickets, regardless of Ferrari's interest in hiring him.
Hamilton, for his part, certainly does not appear to be interested.

When Sky Sports reporter Craig Slater pointed out on Saturday evening in Baku that Horner had effectively raised his hand and put himself in the frame for Ferrari, and asked Hamilton whether he still believed the team was on the right path under Vasseur, the answer was brief, but unequivocal: "Yes."

The fact is that Ferrari has been in contact with Horner on several occasions in the past. In 2010, the idea was reportedly to lure him from Milton Keynes to Maranello as part of a package deal with Adrian Newey. And the carefully chosen wording of his The Times interview certainly suggests that he would clearly be interested should Ferrari ever decide to push the panic button and release Vasseur from his contract.

According to Sky Germany pundit Timo Glock, he believes the comments have put Vasseur in an unnecessarily awkward position: "Vasseur has brought Ferrari back to where they are now. He has brought structure and order into the team. To replace him now and start the next wave of upheaval would, strategically speaking, be completely wrong from Ferrari's point of view."
Even if Ferrari really were contemplating getting rid of Vasseur, why hand the reins to Horner of all people?

The 52-year-old would presumably cost a small fortune — at least by the standards of salaried employment — and he could hardly offer any guarantee of success either. Horner also remains a divisive figure following the allegations made against him during his final years at Red Bull. The boos that greeted him at the O2 Arena during Formula 1's season-launch show in early 2025 showed that he remained a polarising figure among some fans.

Vasseur has made clear that the speculation is becoming a distraction: "Mr Horner is looking for a job. That everybody knows. Everywhere." And: "It's not easy to work with this mood and this atmosphere and to have 25 times a day the same question. For me, for everybody in the team, it's a lack of serenity."

That is exactly what Vasseur and Ferrari should be given now. A public reaffirmation of Vasseur from Ferrari leadership would likely reduce the speculation. Perhaps John Elkann would be well advised to pick up the phone to La Gazzetta dello Sport to set the record straight; that would put a lid on this tiresome Horner story rather quickly.
I don't believe Hamilton is currently losing any sleep over Horner, anyway. There are enough other reasons for that.

Whatever slim chance remained of somehow becoming world champion in 2026 is now largely mathematical. And while Ferrari may conceivably be capable, on the aerodynamic side, of building Formula 1's best car before too long, closing the gap to Mercedes in the power unit department will probably take longer. Even Vasseur himself admits as much.
And plenty of things are going well for Hamilton.

In Barcelona, he proved that even on the other side of 40 he is still capable of winning grands prix. He sits third in the world championship, exactly 20 points ahead of his team-mate Charles Leclerc in fifth. His 2026 form has answered some of the criticism that followed his 2025 season.
And yet, in interviews, his public comments have nevertheless often remained frustrated despite the improved results.
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

The pattern repeats itself from week to week: during races, Hamilton delivers radio messages that could quite reasonably be interpreted as irritated. Later, in front of TV cameras, he spends minutes talking about everything that went wrong, before adding almost as an afterthought that everything inside Ferrari is perfectly fine.
Then, one week later, at the next grand prix media day, he wonders how those journalists could possibly have misunderstood him so badly.

After Baku, he complained about Ferrari's lack of top speed, mentioned a poor start — something Ferrari had been performing better in at the beginning of the season — saying the team must not lie to itself, and pointed out that McLaren and Red Bull had made greater progress. It had simply been "a pretty bad" race, he said. And on top of everything else, he could not get the tyres up to temperature. Already on Saturday, he had complained about "these stupid tyres", calling them "such a pain in the arse": "We've got to bring back some good tyres."
Maybe it's just me - but somehow, Hamilton and Ferrari does not yet feel like one of motorsport's great love stories.
Hamilton, there can be no question, is one of Formula 1's most successful drivers.
Will there be another championship for Hamilton? Can Ferrari give him a realistic chance of an eighth title? I remain sceptical.
keyPointsZh: 霍纳在《泰晤士报》采访中说，他即便余生不再工作也能生活无忧，但仍渴望再尝试一次F1。
文章指出，即使到了2026年巴库站，也没有多少迹象表明霍纳入主法拉利这一情景正在成形。
2021年阿布扎比站时，若有人预测汉密尔顿日后会在霍纳手下为法拉利效力，几乎不会有人当真。
keyPointsEn: In his interview with The Times, Horner said he can comfortably afford never to work another day in his life, yet still feels the urge to give Formula 1 another go.
The article notes that even as of Baku 2026, there is little evidence the scenario of Horner taking over at Ferrari is taking concrete shape.
Had anyone predicted in Abu Dhabi 2021 that Hamilton would one day race for Ferrari under Horner, few would have taken it seriously.

items.titleZh: 谁睡得最好：劳朗·梅基斯
items.summaryZh: Motorsport.com撰文指出，红牛本赛季首次包揽双领奖台，令车队领队劳朗·梅基斯对现状感到满意，而与克里斯蒂安·霍纳乃至最终与赫尔穆特·马尔科分道扬镳，是顺应不同时代所需领导力的果断决定。

media.altZh: 谁睡得最好：劳朗·梅基斯 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: Who slept best last night: Laurent Mekies
items.summaryEn: Motorsport.com argues that Red Bull's first double podium of the year vindicates team boss Laurent Mekies, and that parting ways with Christian Horner and eventually Helmut Marko reflected the need for different leaders in different times.
detailZh: 昨晚谁睡得最好：洛朗·梅基斯
红牛今年首次双车登上领奖台，并不是这位车队老板对目前局势感到满意的唯一原因。
不同的时代需要不同的领导者。
与克里斯蒂安·霍纳分道扬镳，最终又与赫尔穆特·马尔科分手，是一个大胆的举动——毕竟红牛曾凭借这两位从零打造出冠军之师的人取得过无数成功。
也许这正是问题的关键所在。红牛已经变成了一个类似马蜂窝的地方，内部政治、权力斗争接连不断，关键人物一个接一个地离开。重建一支车队所需要的领导者，与组建这支车队的领导者是完全不同的类型。
洛朗·梅基斯与这支车队的缔造者们可谓截然不同。这位法国人冷静、圆融、理性，而且似乎总是面带微笑，毫无疑问，他为红牛展现了一副非常不同的面貌。也许这种评价过于简单化了，毕竟你只有真正与他共事才能真正了解他。但我们现在已经可以开始看出，梅基斯正试图在这支一级方程式最成功的车队之一中培养一种什么样的文化。
当红牛在去年下半年重新开始赢得胜利时，梅基斯经常被问到，在本赛季初期的艰难开局之后，他认为自己个人对这种进步贡献了多少。他的回答往往是“零”，或者接近于零。他当时到任的时间还太短，还不足以产生多大影响。
有人会说，这人多好啊。也有人可能会说，他受过太多的公关训练了。
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队；伊萨克·哈贾尔，红牛车队
现在已经没有人真正再问他那个问题了。
红牛在2026年的进步有多少要归功于梅基斯，这一点依然无法量化。车队目前的处境确实比赛季初要好，而且可以这样说不算过分：即使红牛没有赢得这场研发竞赛，它至少在与迈凯伦并驾齐驱。最新一次升级让红牛在巴库拿到了本赛季首次双车登上领奖台，维斯塔潘距离胜利只差0.196秒。相比维斯塔潘和伊萨克·哈贾尔在中国站或日本站时的表现，这已经是相当大的进步。
其实一段时间以来已经出现了迹象。自从红牛在奥地利引入升级套件以来，只要维斯塔潘完成了大奖赛，他就登上了领奖台。尽管有两次未能完赛，但在这段时间里他的得分只比兰多·诺里斯少5分。
当然，红牛在2026赛季的首场胜利还有待到来。还有很多问题需要解决，包括维斯塔潘公开谈论过的神秘的赛车行为。
尽管缺少奖杯，但今年米凯斯个人已经取得了几场胜利。
留住维斯塔潘是最明显的一场胜利。是的，也许新合同里多出的几个零起到了帮助。但这也是一位就在几个月前还公开讨论自己到底还想在一级方程式中继续多久，而不仅仅是想为哪支车队效力的车手。
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，洛朗·米凯斯，红牛车队领队
米基斯为红牛保住了其最重要的资产，多留了一段时间。维斯塔潘之所以愿意承诺续约，大概是因为他相信红牛能够重新回到经常夺冠的状态。维持这种信念，正是米基斯工作的重要部分。
然而，哈贾尔在巴库登上领奖台，或许才是最能体现米基斯处事方式的例子。这个周末哈贾尔不仅仅是重返工作岗位。他还带着一份全新的2027年红牛合同带来的安心感回归。周三，当他坐上巴库新闻发布厅里那张大得出奇的红色沙发时，他有不少令人愉快的话题可谈——首要的就是他的未来已经尘埃落定。
赛后，米基斯承认在哈贾尔复出之前就公布续约是有意为之。红牛只是想卸掉他身上的一些压力，并向他展示车队对他的信任有多深。对于坐在一级方程式历史上压力最大的那个车席上的车手来说，这一点值得注意。
哈贾尔此前因伤缺阵。他自己也承认，这次受伤是在练拳击时造成的。红牛完全可以先观察他伤愈复出后的表现，再决定是否与他签约。但车队实际上等于对他说：我们相信你。这个车席是你的。你已经证明得足够多了。也许当人们知道自己被重视时，确实会有更好的表现。
哈贾尔本人承认，他在巴库刻意放慢了节奏。最初他的首要任务就是不去撞到任何东西。直到后来他才开始冒险，逐渐建立信心，直到在排位赛中真正全力推进。随后他奉献了可以说是其一级方程式生涯中最出色的一场比赛。
如果在红牛旧的管理体制下，情况可能大不相同。在劳森于他缺席期间表现不俗之后，哈贾尔或许会带着对其未来的疑问回归。也许还会有人公开评论在拳击运动中受伤是否明智。哈贾尔或许会觉得必须立刻证明一切。
当然，这只是猜测。但驾驶第二辆红牛赛车的许多车手都恰好陷入了这样的恶性循环：一个早期的失误带来压力，压力又导致另一个失误，突然间一切都变得更加艰难。事后看来，在巴库站之前就给哈贾尔一份合同，堪称一步妙棋。
关于他在第二次效力红牛时的表现与第一次相比有何不同，已经有很多讨论，每个人都可以自由选择自己偏好的解释。但人们不禁会想，环境是否也起到了一定作用。两次的情况并非完全不同。劳森再次被扔进一辆不熟悉的赛车中，只参加有限几场比赛。但这一次，他看起来判若两人。
也许，当你并不觉得自己非得在一场比赛、一节练习与排位或一圈之内证明一切时，把工作继续推进下去反而更容易——尤其是当再也没有一位刻薄的奥地利老板会在第二天早上六点打电话告诉你“你一无是处”的时候。
这些并不意味着梅基斯是比霍纳或马尔科更好的领导者。这么说会很荒谬。在他们两人的掌管下，红牛几乎赢下了所有能赢的东西。梅基斯要取得哪怕他们成就的一小部分，还有大量工作要做。
但领导一支一级方程式车队并没有唯一正确的方式。也许巴库站提供了又一个信号，表明我们正开始理解梅基斯治下的红牛是什么样子。
同样值得记住的是，尽管霍纳对车队的影响力正在减弱，他的遗产并没有消失。红牛的前任老板自己那个周六大概过得相当愉快——看着老东家的赛车在巴库2.2公里的大直道上飞驰，速度几乎比任何其他赛车都快。
在米尔顿凯恩斯建立红牛动力系统部门，毕竟是霍纳最大的一次豪赌之一。如今梅基斯本人将这台动力单元形容为“出色”，而国际汽联现行的评价体系也实际上将其认定为标杆——尽管这个体系本身可能颇为奇怪。
霍纳大概也很享受赛后浏览新闻的时光。
他的名字出现在瓦塞尔的话语中，瓦塞尔承认，在围绕他自身前途的持续猜测中，法拉利“并非在完全平静的氛围中工作”。尽管瓦塞尔在媒体见面会上努力开玩笑、谈笑风生，但霍纳最近接受《泰晤士报》的采访显然惹恼了他——而惹恼其他一级方程式车队领队，似乎一直是霍纳乐在其中的事情。
梅基斯与霍纳的故事或许还会出现一个有趣的转折。法拉利车队领队一职，无疑是梅基斯在马拉内罗工作那些年里必然渴望得到的。他最终没有得到便离开了法拉利，经由小红牛车队，反倒成了红牛的掌门人。如今霍纳——那位梅基斯最终继承了其旧职的人——却与梅基斯从未得到的法拉利职位联系在了一起。也许这两人的纠葛还没完。
这仍然是一个相当疯狂、令人难以想象的局面。但不同的时代需要不同的领导者。
红牛决定，它的下一个篇章需要的是一个面带微笑的法国人，而不是一个咄咄逼人、擅长政治手腕的英国人。也许终有一天，法拉利会决定它需要的恰恰相反。
detailEn: Who slept best last night: Laurent Mekies
Red Bull’s first double podium of the year isn’t the only reason for its boss to be satisfied with how things are going
Different times require different leaders.
Parting ways with Christian Horner, and eventually Helmut Marko, was a bold move after all the success Red Bull enjoyed with the duo who built the squad from scratch into a title-winning machine.

Perhaps that was the point. Red Bull had become something of a wasps’ nest, with internal politics, power struggles and key people leaving one after another. Rebuilding a team requires a very different kind of leader than one who assembles it.

Laurent Mekies could hardly be more different from the team's creators. Calm, diplomatic, rational and seemingly always smiling, the Frenchman certainly presents a very different face for Red Bull. An overly simplistic assessment of someone you’d really have to work with to understand, maybe. But we're now starting to see what kind of culture Mekies is trying to cultivate at one of Formula 1's most successful teams.

When Red Bull started winning again in the second half of last year, Mekies was often asked how much he thought he personally had contributed to that progress after a difficult start to the season. His answer was often "zero", or close to it. He simply hadn’t been there long enough to influence much.
What a nice guy, some would say. Too well PR-trained, others might argue.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing
Nobody really asks him that question anymore.

How much of Red Bull’s progress in 2026 is down to Mekies remains impossible to quantify. It is certainly in a better place than at the start of the season, and it’s probably not unreasonable to suggest that, if Red Bull isn’t winning the development race, it is at least keeping pace with McLaren in that field. Its latest upgrade delivered Red Bull’s first double podium of the season in Baku, with Max Verstappen missing victory by just 0.196s. Compared to where Verstappen and Isack Hadjar were in China or Japan, that is quite some progress.

There have been signs for a while. Since Red Bull’s Austria package was introduced, whenever Verstappen has finished a grand prix he has been on the podium. Despite two non-finishes, he has scored only five points fewer than Lando Norris over that period.
The first win of the 2026 season for Red Bull is still to come, of course. There are plenty of issues to sort out too, including mysterious car behaviours Verstappen has openly discussed.
Despite a lack of trophies, there have already been a couple of victories for Mekies personally this year.

Keeping Verstappen was the most obvious one. Yes, perhaps a few extra zeroes in a new contract helped. But this is also a driver who only a few months ago was openly discussing how long he even wanted to continue in Formula 1, rather than merely which team he wanted to drive for.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Team Principal

Mekies has secured Red Bull’s biggest asset for a little longer. Verstappen presumably wouldn’t have committed had he not believed Red Bull could return to winning regularly. Maintaining that belief is very much part of Mekies’ job.

Yet it's Hadjar’s Baku podium that might be the best illustration yet of Mekies’ approach. Hadjar didn’t merely return to his duties this weekend. He returned with the reassurance of a fresh Red Bull contract for 2027. When he landed on the ridiculously large red couch in Baku’s press conference room on Wednesday, he had plenty of pleasant things to discuss — first and foremost the fact that his future was already sorted.

After the race, Mekies acknowledged that announcing Hadjar before his comeback was intentional. Red Bull simply wanted to remove some of the pressure and show him how much it trusted him. That feels noteworthy for a driver occupying what has historically been Formula 1’s ultimate pressure-cooker seat.

Hadjar had been out injured. He has now himself admitted the injury was sustained while boxing. Red Bull could easily have waited to see how he returned before committing to him. Instead, the team effectively told him: we trust you. The seat is yours. You have already proved enough. Perhaps people really do perform better when they know they are valued.

Hadjar himself admitted he deliberately took things slowly in Baku. His priority initially was simply not to hit anything. Only later did he start taking risks, building confidence until he was properly pushing in qualifying. And then he produced arguably the best race of his F1 career.

It could have been different under the old Red Bull regime. Hadjar might instead have returned with questions hanging over his future after Liam Lawson’s decent run in his absence. There might have been public comments about the wisdom of injuring yourself while boxing. Perhaps Hadjar would have felt he needed to prove everything immediately.

That is speculation, of course. But plenty of drivers in that second Red Bull have fallen into precisely that spiral: an early mistake creates pressure, pressure creates another mistake, and suddenly everything becomes harder. Giving Hadjar the contract before Baku looks, in hindsight, like a brilliant move.

Plenty has already been said about how different his second Red Bull stint looked compared to his first, and everyone is free to choose their preferred explanation. But you can’t help wondering whether the environment played a part. The circumstances weren’t entirely dissimilar. Lawson was again thrown into an unfamiliar car for a limited number of races. This time, though, he looked like a different driver.

Perhaps it is simply easier to get on with the job when you don’t feel the desperate need to prove everything in one race, one session or one lap — and when there is no prospect of a nasty Austrian boss calling you at 6am the following morning to inform you that you’re useless.

None of this means Mekies is a better leader than Horner or Marko. That would be ridiculous to state. With both of them in charge, Red Bull won almost everything there was to win. Mekies still has an enormous amount to do before he can claim even a fraction of their achievements.
But there is no single correct way to lead a Formula 1 team. And perhaps Baku offered another indication that we are beginning to understand what Mekies’ Red Bull looks like.

It is also worth remembering that, while his influence on the team is growing, Horner’s legacy hasn’t disappeared. Red Bull’s former boss probably had quite an enjoyable Saturday himself, watching the cars of his former team fly down Baku’s 2.2km straight faster than pretty much anything else.

Building Red Bull Powertrains in Milton Keynes was, after all, one of Horner’s biggest gambles. Now Mekies himself describes the resulting power unit as “fantastic”, while the FIA’s current system has effectively identified it as the benchmark - however peculiar that system might be.
Horner probably enjoyed browsing the news after the race too.

His name appeared in quotes from Fred Vasseur, who admitted Ferrari was “not working in perfect serenity” amid the constant speculation over his own future. As much as Vasseur tried to joke and laugh during his media session, Horner had clearly managed to annoy him with his recent interview with The Times - and annoying other F1 team bosses was always something Horner appeared to enjoy enormously.

And there could yet be an amusing twist to the Mekies-Horner story. The Ferrari team principal role is one Mekies himself would surely have coveted during his years at Maranello. He eventually left Ferrari without getting it and, via Racing Bulls, ended up in charge of Red Bull instead. Now Horner - the man whose old job Mekies ultimately inherited — is being linked with the Ferrari position Mekies never got. Perhaps the two haven't finished with each other yet.
It remains a pretty wild scenario to contemplate. But different times require different leaders.
Red Bull decided its next chapter needed a smiling Frenchman rather than an aggressive and political Englishman. It may still be that one day Ferrari decides it needs the opposite.

items.originalTitle: Isack Hadjar earns "team-mate points" after "exceptional comeback" in Baku, says Alex Brundle
items.summaryEn: According to F1 TV pundit Alex Brundle, Red Bull's Isack Hadjar delivered an exceptional comeback drive to third place at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix after returning from a wrist injury, earning crucial team-mate points for his team.
detailZh: 亚历克斯·布伦德尔表示，哈贾尔在巴库完成“极其出色的逆转”后，赢得了“队友积分”。
哈贾尔在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上上演了一场令人印象深刻的逆转，最终获得第三名，因此获得了亚历克斯·布伦德尔的称赞。
据F1电视评论员亚历克斯·布伦德尔称，红牛车队的哈贾尔在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上凭借一场“极其出色的逆转”拿到第三名，赢得了关键的“队友积分”。
哈贾尔此前因手腕受伤缺席比赛，如今带着一份新签下的2027年红牛合同重返驾驶舱，他利用迈凯伦车手皮亚斯特里在比赛末段锁死轮胎的机会，与获得第二名的维斯塔潘一起，为位于米尔顿凯恩斯的车队斩获了双车登上领奖台的成绩。
在F1电视的赛后节目中，布伦德尔称赞了哈贾尔的速度，以及当他被要求保持在队友身后位置时服从车队指令的意愿。
"这样或那样，我认为马克斯在比赛结束时仍然会大幅领先哈贾尔，"布伦德尔解释道。"而且从比赛的进程来看，当他换上软胎时，他很可能很快就会超过哈贾尔。
"但哈贾尔今天确实完成了一场非凡的逆袭，他顾全大局的表现为他赢得了不少队友好感分，而且他这个周末展现出了惊人的速度。
"如果你想带着一份新合同从伤病中实现回归，那就是最理想的回归方式，他完全配得上领奖台。事实上，作为一对车手组合，他们是今天全场最出色的。
1996年一级方程式世界冠军达蒙·希尔也加入了布伦德尔的转播解说，他补充道："伊萨克·哈贾尔在受伤并离开赛场之后还能如此强势地回归，真是令人难以置信的恢复。他们是一支强大的车队。你永远不能低估红牛。"
"他们是一支敢于进攻、勇于冒险的车队，总是抓住机会。他们一直在为各种目标而战，令人惊叹。必须承认，他们经历了这么多不同批次的管理层变动，还有天知道的其他什么折腾，但他们依然在坚持战斗。"
维斯塔潘和哈贾尔目前在车手积分榜上分列第六和第八位，分别拥有163分和86分。因此，红牛在车队积分榜上排名第四，积分是263分，其中包括利亚姆·劳森在顶替受伤的哈贾尔参赛期间所获得的分数。
detailEn: Isack Hadjar earns "team-mate points" after "exceptional comeback" in Baku, says Alex Brundle
Isack Hadjar earned praise from Alex Brundle after delivering an impressive comeback drive to third at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix
Red Bull's Isack Hadjar earned crucial "team-mate points" following an "exceptional comeback" drive to third at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, according to F1 TV pundit Alex Brundle.

Returning to the cockpit after a wrist injury with a newly signed Red Bull contract for 2027, Hadjar capitalised on a late lock-up from McLaren's Oscar Piastri to secure a double podium for the Milton Keynes outfit alongside second-place finisher Max Verstappen.
Speaking on F1 TV's post-race broadcast, Brundle praised Hadjar's pace and willingness to follow team orders when told to remain in position behind his team-mate.

"This way or that way, I think Max would have ended up generously ahead of Hadjar at the end of the race," Brundle explained. "And as it played out, he probably would have passed him pretty quickly when he was on the soft tyre.
"But Hadjar really had an exceptional comeback today and has earned himself some good team-mate points for playing the game and he demonstrated amazing pace this weekend.

"If you want to have a comeback from an injury with a new contract in your hands, that's the one to have, and he thoroughly deserved the podium. In fact, as a pair of drivers, the best in the field today."

1996 Formula 1 champion Damon Hill, who joined Brundle on the broadcast, added: "Incredible recovery from Isack Hadjar to bounce back after his injury and being away. They were a strong team. You can never discount Red Bull.

"They are an aggressive attacking racing team who take chances. They're always fighting for things, and they're incredible. You have to say they've been through so many different iterations of management and goodness knows what, but they're still there fighting."

Verstappen and Hadjar currently sit sixth and eighth in the drivers' championship with 163 points and 86 points, respectively. As a result, Red Bull is fourth in the constructors' standings with 263 points, which includes the points that Liam Lawson scored while stepping in for the injured Hadjar.
